chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The adulterer marries not except an adulteress or an idolatress.'
He said: 'These were women well-known for adultery and men well-known for adultery, who were recognized by that, and the people today are in that same status.'
So whoever upon whom the legal penalty for adultery has been established, or who is publicized for it, it is not befitting for anyone to marry him until repentance is recognized from him.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'The adulterer marries not except an adulteress' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Quranic term 'zani' in verse 24:3 refers specifically to those publicly known for adultery or upon whom the hadd penalty has been established, rather than every individual who commits the act. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on public reputation (shuhrat) as the criterion for the marriage prohibition, which remains in effect until genuine repentance is verified.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [24:3] And the adulterer shall not marry any but a adulteress or an idolatress,
so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘These were women well known with the adultery and men well known with the adultery. They were recognised with that, and the people today are with that status.
So the one upon whom a Legal Penalty (Hadd) has been established, or publicised with it, it is not befitting for anyone that he should marry him until the repentance is recognised from him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the word of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘A prostitute man cannot marry but a prostitute woman or a pagan.’ [24:4]
He (the Imam) said, ‘They were well-known prostitute females and males.
Today people who are convicted for fornication and punished (by the qualified court) are of the same status. No one must marry them unless it is known that they have repented.’”
